section_summary: This section contains charts of Japanese securities sold by liquidation bodies from 1946 through February 1948, followed by correspondence explaining the sales. It also documents a 1948 sterling payments arrangement for Japan’s trade, India’s and Ceylon’s participation, controls on Japanese government spending, discussion of a possible sterling loan, and circulation of an export-import loan agreement.

subfiles.title: Securities sold by the Closed Institutions Liquidation Commission, Chart No. 1
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese share offerings through June 1947, including sale methods, buyers, unsold shares and proceeds.
subfiles.summary: The chart continues a company-by-company register of securities offered by the Closed Institutions Liquidation Commission before the Securities Coordinating Liquidation Committee began operating. Paired pages list issuers and offering details, then sales and proceeds; the final pages give totals. Several pages are duplicated or out of sequence in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Securities sold by the Securities Coordinating Liquidating Committee, Chart No. 2
subfiles.from: Securities Coordinating Liquidating Committee
subfiles.about: Records security offerings and sales from July 1947 to February 1948.
subfiles.summary: The chart lists issuers, selling agencies, dates, methods of offering, numbers of buyers, shares sold and unsold, and proceeds. It includes holdings attributed to liquidation commissions, the state and the Bank of Japan. Its closing total reports 4,978,323 shares offered, 4,363,236 sold and 615,087 unsold, with proceeds of ¥384,992,213.80; some chart pages are duplicated in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Army transmittal of report on securities sales
subfiles.from: Department of the Army, Reports and Analysis Branch
subfiles.to: Walter C. Hulick, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on securities sold by the two liquidation commissions.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the securities sales report for State Department retention.

subfiles.title: Sale of securities by the liquidation commissions
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Chief, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Explains the accompanying securities sales charts and remaining holdings.
subfiles.summary: Explains the two charts, states that sales now pass through the coordinating committee, and estimates securities still to be sold.

subfiles.title: Currency arrangement between Japan and the Sterling Area
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the new sterling payments agreement for Japan’s trade with participating countries.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards the agreement and replies exchanged with the United Kingdom Liaison Mission. He describes sterling accounts, dollar conversion rules, the exception for certain cotton textiles, settlement of open accounts, and the agreement’s effect from May 31, 1948.

subfiles.title: Duplicate first page of Despatch No. 334
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats the opening page of the sterling arrangement despatch.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate opening page of Despatch No. 334.

subfiles.title: United Kingdom proposal for payments arrangements, Enclosure No. 1
subfiles.from: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets proposed terms for sterling accounts, conversion, participating countries and termination.
subfiles.summary: The surviving continuation pages set out six-month conversion dates, Bank of England exchange rates, treatment of outstanding credits, settlement of open accounts, and each participant’s right to withdraw on notice. They list participating Sterling Area territories and propose that the exchange of memoranda constitute the agreement. The first page of this enclosure is absent from the supplied sequence.

subfiles.title: Duplicate securities chart page
subfiles.about: Repeats a page of share sales and proceeds figures.
subfiles.summary: Duplicated sales and proceeds table, apparently displaced from Chart No. 2.

subfiles.title: SCAP memorandum confirming payments arrangements, Enclosure No. 3
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Head, United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Confirms the overall sterling payments agreement replacing the interim private-trade arrangement.
subfiles.summary: SCAP accepts sterling settlement for trade with participating Sterling Area countries, except specified cotton textiles made from U.S. cotton. The memorandum defines bank accounts, conversion to dollars, the June and December conversion dates, treatment of credits, settlement of open accounts and termination. Its heading is noisy in the OCR; the enclosing despatch identifies this reply as dated May 29.

subfiles.title: India’s and Ceylon’s participation in the sterling arrangement
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards notices and acknowledgments of India’s and Ceylon’s participation.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reports that both governments joined retroactively from May 31, 1948. It highlights an exception preserving India’s existing trade contract and open account.

subfiles.title: India’s participation in sterling payments arrangements
subfiles.from: H. H. Thomas, United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Notifies India’s participation while reserving its existing contract and open account.
subfiles.summary: India joins, subject to its existing contract; the open-account settlement clause does not apply.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of India’s participation
subfiles.from: F. E. Pickelle, Foreign Trade and Commerce Division
subfiles.to: Head, United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Accepts India’s participation and confirms the exception for its existing contract.
subfiles.summary: SCAP accepts India’s participation effective May 31 and preserves its contractual open account.

subfiles.title: Ceylon’s participation in sterling payments arrangements
subfiles.from: E. R. Lingeman, United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Notifies Ceylon’s decision to participate retroactively from May 31.
subfiles.summary: Ceylon confirms participation in the sterling payments arrangement from May 31, 1948.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Ceylon’s participation
subfiles.from: F. E. Pickelle, Foreign Trade and Commerce Division
subfiles.to: Head, United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: Accepts Ceylon’s retroactive participation in the sterling arrangement.
subfiles.summary: SCAP accepts Ceylon’s participation effective May 31, 1948.

subfiles.title: Transmission of staff memorandum on Japanese government financing
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a February staff memorandum that may not have been sent previously.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Staff Memorandum No. 8 on Japanese government financing.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government Financing, Staff Memorandum No. 8
subfiles.from: Paul J. Mueller, Chief of Staff, SCAP and Far East Command
subfiles.about: Directs staff to restrain Japanese government expenditures to counter inflation.
subfiles.summary: Orders minimum spending and Economic and Scientific Section review of proposed fiscal actions.

subfiles.title: Contemplated sterling loan to Japan
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Reports a House of Commons exchange on a possible sterling loan to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The airgram reproduces parliamentary questions and answers. Douglas Jay says no final decision is expected before commercial banks consider specific proposals and that U.S. European Recovery Program aid does not itself bar a sterling loan. Members raise trade effects, reparations and earlier loan claims.

subfiles.title: Assistant Secretary’s note on release of loan agreement
subfiles.from: Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Notes State and Army agreement to release an Export-Import Bank agreement to FEC members.
subfiles.summary: State and Army have no objection; the bank requests an exchange of letters.

subfiles.title: Note forwarding proposed letter to Export-Import Bank
subfiles.from: C. C. I.
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposed letter for Saltzman’s signature with background papers.
subfiles.summary: Requests review and forwarding of the draft letter and attachments.

subfiles.title: Proposed letter to Export-Import Bank on releasing the May 13 agreement
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.to: W. McC. Martin Jr., Chairman, Export-Import Bank
subfiles.about: Seeks written concurrence to distribute the May 13 loan agreement to Far Eastern Commission members.
subfiles.summary: The draft says State supports distributing the agreement and exhibits concerning the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund and an American bank consortium. It records that interested U.S. agencies have no objection, notes the agreement is unclassified but would be circulated as restricted, and asks the bank to confirm before release.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Secretariat note on loan agreement
subfiles.from: F. Turner, Far Eastern Commission Secretariat
subfiles.about: Asks whether the $60 million May 13 loan agreement may be released to FEC delegations.
subfiles.summary: India presses for release; Turner seeks State and Army views.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for letter from Baar, Bennett & Fullen
subfiles.from: Anson W. Bartlett
subfiles.about: Forwards an August 17 letter for division consideration.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the attached letter following a conversation with Noel Hemmendinger.
